module_title: Parliament - Sessions, Bills, and Special Powers
introduction: At this level, we explore how Parliament functions through its sessions, the process of law-making (types of bills), the concept of Joint Sittings, and the exclusive powers held independently by the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.

core_concepts.title: Sessions of Parliament
core_concepts.description: The President summons each House. The maximum gap between two sessions cannot be more than 6 months. Usually, there are three sessions: Budget Session (Feb-May), Monsoon Session (July-Sep), and Winter Session (Nov-Dec).

core_concepts.title: Money Bill (Article 110)
core_concepts.description: A bill dealing exclusively with taxation, borrowing, or the Consolidated Fund of India. It can be introduced ONLY in the Lok Sabha and ONLY on the prior recommendation of the President. The Speaker decides if a bill is a Money Bill.

core_concepts.title: Joint Sitting (Article 108)
core_concepts.description: If there is a deadlock between the two Houses over an Ordinary Bill, the President can summon a Joint Sitting. It is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (NOT the Chairman/VP).

core_concepts.title: Special Powers of Lok Sabha
core_concepts.description: 1. Money Bills can originate only here. 2. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible ONLY to the Lok Sabha. 3. A No-Confidence Motion can only be introduced here.

core_concepts.title: Special Powers of Rajya Sabha
core_concepts.description: 1. It can authorize Parliament to make a law on a State List subject (Article 249). 2. It can authorize Parliament to create a new All-India Service (Article 312).

important_entities.name: Speaker of Lok Sabha
important_entities.key_fact: Final Deciding Authority on Money Bills
important_entities.significance: Their decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final and cannot be questioned in any court or by the President.

important_entities.name: Quorum
important_entities.significance: It is 1/10th of the total strength of the House (55 for LS, 25 for RS). Without a quorum, the presiding officer must suspend the meeting.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Rajya Sabha's role in Money Bills
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject a Money Bill. It can only make recommendations and must return the bill within 14 days. If it doesn't, the bill is deemed passed.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: No Joint Sitting for certain Bills
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A Joint Sitting (Article 108) CANNOT be called for a Money Bill or a Constitutional Amendment Bill (Art 368). These bills must be passed by both houses separately.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Budget, Monsoon, Winter. (Arranged in chronological order of occurrence in a year).

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC and State PCS frequently ask: 'Who presides over the joint sitting?' The answer is the Speaker of Lok Sabha. (If absent, Deputy Speaker of LS, then Deputy Chairman of RS. The VP never presides).
Identify the difference between Prorogation (end of a session by President) and Adjournment (end of a sitting by Speaker/Chairman).
